a membrane-inserted polypeptide is degraded in eukaryotic cell by an endocytosis-dependent process.
a membrane-inserted polypeptide is rapidly degraded by a process that involves endocytosis, transport to lysosomes, and protease cleavage.
a membrane-inserted, cleaved diphtheria B-fragment is removed by a process that requires endocytosis, ATP hydrolysis, and acidification.

the fate of a protein that is inserted into the plasma membrane.
the mechanisms of membrane insertion and removal of foreign polypeptides.
the study of the fate of a membrane-inserting polypeptide after insertion into the eukaryotic plasma membrane.

the diphthera toxin B-fragment is inserted into the membrane of the cell, and then endocytosed into the cell, where it is degraded.
